7.speaker: Lucian Galade
7.text: “My efforts to ensure a court rejection for the legal arguments put forward by Mr. Ricter are continuing.”

8.speaker: Lucian Galade
8.text: “What are you leaning towards? How should we move forward?”

9.speaker: Lucian Galade
9.text: “It's true, we are in the hornet's nest if we can't get out of this situation. But they want us to seize the assets of the Oligarchs, an action that would drastically alter the power balance.”

10.speaker: Player
10.text: “The Court needs to pass that review for us to continue uninterrupted. The decree must be deemed constitutional. Otherwise, we are weakened.”

12.speaker: Player
12.text: “Our administration will avoid upsetting the economic structure and maintain the status quo.”

13.speaker: Lucian Galade
13.text: “I have to ask. Why? What is your intention?”

14.speaker: Lucian Galade
14.text: “I have to ask. Why? What is your intention?”

15.speaker: Narrator
15.text: Lucian took a note in his notebook.

19.speaker: Lucian Galade
19.text: “Changing the ownership of some of these assets would increase our budget even more.”

20.speaker: Lucian Galade
20.text: “The plan to change the ownership of important assets could help us generate much needed resources to further improve economic development before the next election.”

22.speaker: Narrator
22.text: He arrived on time as usual and took his seat right across from me.

24.speaker: Narrator
24.text: Lucian had dark circles below his eyes. The plethora of political developments must've been weighing even on a workaholic like him.

25.speaker: Player
25.text: “You look a bit tired. Are you getting enough sleep?”

31.speaker: Lucian Galade
31.text: “I must say, you don't look much better.”

32.speaker: Narrator
32.text: I looked at myself in a small hand mirror. Similar circles were beneath my eyes as well.

33.speaker: Lucian Galade
33.text: “I booked some of your time to pre-plan for today's meeting at the Ministry of Economy.”

34.speaker: Lucian Galade
34.text: “I want to give you a short status update.”

35.speaker: Lucian Galade
35.text: “A very important piece in succeeding will be this upcoming economy meeting.”

36.speaker: Lucian Galade
36.text: “It is well known that the Old Guard wants many of these large companies to be nationalized. If we do that, our chances of the court rejecting Mr. Ricter will increase.”

37.speaker: Lucian Galade
37.text: “As you know, I've been lobbying the Old Guard extensively after the constitutional review process began to ensure we don't end up in a weakened position.”

38.speaker: Player
38.text: “That makes sense. I will think about it.”

39.speaker: Player
39.text: “I won't let the Old Guard decide the future of our country in any way.”

40.speaker: Player
40.text: “I will do what I want. It's as simple as that.”

42.speaker: Lucian Galade
42.text: “While I agree, it doesn't change the fact that if they accept Mr. Ricter's plea, we might be done for.”

44.speaker: Lucian Galade
44.text: “We would be changing our relationship with the Old Guard, the Oligarchs and the opposition.”

45.speaker: Lucian Galade
45.text: “We need to be cautious. Any grand plans about the economy also heavily influence our political standing.”

46.speaker: Lucian Galade
46.text: "As you know, this meeting will give you the opportunity to alter the ownership of the Big Four, the corporations at the center of Sordland's ownership question."

47.speaker: Lucian Galade
47.text: “I personally think we should stay out of this and keep things as they are. There is no need to make new political enemies at this stage in our term.”

49.speaker: Lucian Galade
49.text: “It's true that the more control we have, the better. Your administration still bears responsibility If we let the Oligarchs determine the course of the country.”

50.speaker: Player
50.text: “I cannot allow a major part of the country to run without my input as President. The Oligarchs must submit to me.”

51.speaker: Player
51.text: “Truth to be told, I don't care what anyone thinks or says. I will do what I believe in.”

55.speaker: Player
55.text: “If we want to improve our relations with the east, we need to nationalize our economy.”

56.speaker: Lucian Galade
56.text: “It's true that Valgsland would look very favorably on such changes in any upcoming negotiations. And United Contana would see it as a positive step towards a potential membership in the CSP.”

60.speaker: Lucian Galade
60.text: “I understand. However, we need to think carefully about the effects of your actions. Especially since the next election is getting closer every day.”

64.speaker: Player
64.text: “If we want to improve our relations with the west, we need to privatize our economy.”

65.speaker: Player
65.text: “Privatisation will help bring the country out of recession.”

66.speaker: Player
66.text: “Truth to be told I don't care what anyone thinks or says. I will do what I believe in.”

67.speaker: Lucian Galade
67.text: “I understand, but we need to think carefully about the effects of your actions. Especially with the elections getting closer every day."

68.speaker: Lucian Galade
68.text: “That may be true. But taking everything out of state hands may have dire repercussions in a country like ours. We need to think about this carefully.”

69.speaker: Lucian Galade
69.text: “It's true, Lespia would look very favorably on such changes in the upcoming negotiations. Arcasia would see it as a positive step towards membership in the ATO.”

70.speaker: Player
70.text: “The Oligarchs are powerful. They might aid us in Assembly if we help them.”

74.speaker: Lucian Galade
74.text: “It's good to think strategically like that. But if we make them too powerful, they might end up stabbing us in the back. There might be dire repercussions.”

78.speaker: Lucian Galade
78.text: “One thing to remember is that since you've been transparent about promoting a planned economy, nationalization will not cost us much support."

79.speaker: Lucian Galade
79.text: “I have to remind you that nationalization goes against your initial plans for a market economy. We might lose support because of it.”

80.speaker: Lucian Galade
80.text: “One thing to remember is that since you've been transparent about promoting a market economy, privatization will not cost us much support."

84.speaker: Lucian Galade
84.text: “I have to remind you that privatization goes against your initial plans for a planned economy. We might lose support because of it.”

85.speaker: Lucian Galade
85.text: “I received a report from the Ministry of Economy that may impact your decision.”

86.speaker: Lucian Galade
86.text: “We have a large government budget available to improve the economy.”

87.speaker: Lucian Galade
87.text: “Unfortunately we have missed our government budget targets for the current quarter.”

88.speaker: Lucian Galade
88.text: “It's just something to consider. As is our relationship with the Oligarchs.”

89.speaker: Lucian Galade
89.text: “Although I think the Oligarchs would've liked us to privatize everything, maintaining the status quo will not disturb our relationship with them.”

99.speaker: Lucian Galade
99.text: “We might be aiming for nationalization, but we need to remember that they only care about their own profits.”

101.speaker: Lucian Galade
101.text: “Unfortunately, we aren't on good terms with them. This situation has been obstructing some of our efforts in the economic recovery.”

102.speaker: Lucian Galade
102.text: “Thankfully, we are on good terms with them for now, which helps us with the economic recovery.”

111.speaker: Lucian Galade
111.text: “Excellent. This is the safest way to victory.”

112.speaker: Lucian Galade
112.text: “This means more stability. Both economically and politically.”

113.speaker: Lucian Galade
113.text: “If our nationalization plan hurts their assets too much, it can put us at odds with the men who control much of the economy.”

114.speaker: Lucian Galade
114.text: “Walter Tusk seems to be organizing several opposing centrist and liberal Assembly members to back us in the upcoming vote. If we maintain our standing with him, our reforms process will benefit.”

115.speaker: Lucian Galade
115.text: “Walter Tusk seems to be organizing several opposing conservative and nationalist Assembly members to back us in the upcoming vote. If we maintain our standing with him, our reforms process will benefit.”

116.speaker: Player
116.text: “We don't want the Lotherberg Group to be our enemies. It'll endanger our re-election.”

117.speaker: Player
117.text: “If we nationalize only a part of their companies, perhaps we can avoid confrontation.”

118.speaker: Player
118.text: “It's good to know that Tusk is actively supporting our administration.”

119.speaker: Player
119.text: “It's all a show. He and the others won't lift a finger without clear benefit. Besides, we don't need them.”

123.speaker: Player
123.text: “I'm confident that we will overcome the next hurdle without his help.”

124.speaker: Lucian Galade
124.text: “Walter Tusk seems to be organizing several centrist Assembly members to pressure the court on behalf. If we maintain our standing with him, it might positively influence the court decision.”

125.speaker: Lucian Galade
125.text: “If our nationalization plan hurts their assets too much, we may end up at war with the men who control much of the economy.”

129.speaker: Lucian Galade
129.text: “Yes, that's the only kind of nationalization they'd accept. I am sure that Tusk will have further requests afterwards, though.”

130.speaker: Player
130.text: “The Oligarchs must be destroyed. Seizing their assets is the way to go.”

131.speaker: Lucian Galade
131.text: “Just be careful with him. Remember, any path we take here could very well determine what battles we fight in the future.”

132.speaker: Lucian Galade
132.text: “The only way to avoid being damaged by such a dramatic action is a swift surprise takeover."

133.speaker: Lucian Galade
133.text: “Indeed. They have their hands in many pockets, and the last thing we want is another powerful force to fight when our main goal should be to maintain public opinion.”

137.speaker: Player
137.text: “To save our country from recession, privatization is a must.”

149.speaker: Lucian Galade
149.text: “That would certainly be a wise compromise."

150.speaker: Lucian Galade
150.text: “Just be careful with him. Remember, any path we take here could very well determine what battles we fight in the future.”

151.speaker: Lucian Galade
151.text: “If we implement a privatization plan, it will boost our relationship even further.”

152.speaker: Lucian Galade
152.text: “However, if we implement a privatization plan, they would surely be delighted.”

153.speaker: Lucian Galade
153.text: “Still, we need to make sure that we don't go overboard with it. If we do, we might lose our base both in the USP and among the people.”

154.speaker: Lucian Galade
154.text: “Some of my connections indicate that there seems to be a contest for leadership in the Lotherberg Group.”

156.speaker: Lucian Galade
156.text: “It looks like Marcel Koronti is making moves to become the key figure.”

157.speaker: Lucian Galade
157.text: “Koronti probably wants his father's seat as the head of the Group and Tusk doesn't want to let go of it.”

164.speaker: Lucian Galade
164.text: “Because we are going down the path of nationalization, we will have the power to tip the balance towards either side.”

165.speaker: Lucian Galade
165.text: “It's a significant power struggle considering these are the heads of Sordland's two largest private corporations.”

166.speaker: Lucian Galade
166.text: “If we over-privatize our state owned companies, the Sordish State Corporation and Nedam Mining Group, it could result in the balance tipping to one side.”

167.speaker: Lucian Galade
167.text: “Another reason why I am supporting your decision to leave the situation as it is.”

168.speaker: Lucian Galade
168.text: “Since you have already made the decision to nationalize, you need to be decisive in your follow-up actions.”

169.speaker: Lucian Galade
169.text: “They would fight over buying up shares and cause chaos.”

170.speaker: Lucian Galade
170.text: “Since you have already made the decision to privatize, you need to be decisive in your follow-up actions.”

171.speaker: Lucian Galade
171.text: “Our relationship with Walter Tusk hasn't been good so far. Any move we make now has to be calculated and thought through.”

172.speaker: Lucian Galade
172.text: “Our relationship with Walter Tusk has been very strong so far and we have the backing of the Oligarchs thanks to that.”

178.speaker: Player
178.text: “Don't worry. I have it under control.”

179.speaker: Narrator
179.text: Lucian gave me a long, measured look.

180.speaker: Lucian Galade
180.text: “I was sure one of them would contact you.”

181.speaker: Player
181.text: “He wanted to make a deal to leave HOS untouched.”

183.speaker: Lucian Galade
183.text: “Mr. President, if you are not transparent with me, I can't help you to the best of my ability."

184.speaker: Lucian Galade
184.text: “Very well, sir. I won't push you further.”

185.speaker: Player
185.text: “I threatened him with nationalization in return for his support. It worked.”

192.speaker: Player
192.text: “He threatened me, so I told him I'm taking him down.”

194.speaker: Lucian Galade
194.text: “I hope he will keep his word.”

196.speaker: Lucian Galade
196.text: “Never mind whatever I said before. This changes everything.”

197.speaker: Lucian Galade
197.text: “Marcel Koronti is too dangerous and too powerful to have as an enemy. We need to take him down now or we might not get another chance.”

198.speaker: Lucian Galade
198.text: “Mr. President. We need to nationalize HOS.”

199.speaker: Lucian Galade
199.text: “Otherwise, we might not stand a chance of re-election.”

201.speaker: Player
201.text: “Don't worry about it. I have it all under control.”

202.speaker: Lucian Galade
202.text: "All right, sir. I trust you that you will make the best decision.”

206.speaker: Player
206.text: “He also wants me to nationalize Bergia Steel to take down Tusk.”

209.speaker: Lucian Galade
209.text: “At any rate, this internal conflict among the Oligarchs puts us in an interesting position."

210.speaker: Lucian Galade
210.text: “And we need to do it quickly.”

212.speaker: Lucian Galade
212.text: “I will inform Mr. Holl of your decision and he will make the necessary preparations to formulate a plan.”

214.speaker: Lucian Galade
214.text: “We can start the process of nationalization or privatization, or we can just keep the status quo.”

218.speaker: Lucian Galade
218.text: “Very well then. I'll cancel the meeting since we are not taking any actions.”

219.speaker: Lucian Galade
219.text: “I am glad you have made this decision.”

220.speaker: Narrator
220.text: Lucian got up from his chair and left the office.

225.speaker: Lucian Galade
225.text: “There is no reason for us to interfere, directly or indirectly, in their internal struggles.”

227.speaker: Lucian Galade
227.text: “Again, I remind you that any change will tip an already-fragile balance."

229.speaker: Lucian Galade
229.text: “I must get back to work now. See you at the next meeting.”

234.speaker: Player
234.text: “He also wants me to give him the shares from privatization to lower Tusk's influence.”

235.speaker: Lucian Galade
235.text: “Indeed. They have their hands in many pockets, and the last thing we want is another powerful force to fight when our main goal should be to maintain public opinion.”

237.speaker: Lucian Galade
237.text: “This internal conflict among the Oligarchs puts us in an interesting position."

268.speaker: Player
268.text: “I stopped him before he could say anything."

269.speaker: Lucian Galade
269.text: “Not involving ourselves in The Oligarchs businesses will save us from potential headaches."

270.speaker: Lucian Galade
270.text: “But with the decisions, we're about to make today. I doubt that we can stay neutral for long. "

277.speaker: Lucian Galade
277.text: “But before going into the economic direction, I want to give you a short status update.”

284.speaker: Lucian Galade
284.text: "After your supportive statements of Ishval Ersen together with Mr. Ricter, the Supreme Court decided not to act at all, and delayed the case until further notice."

285.speaker: Lucian Galade
285.text: "Moreover, the Bludish community in Bergia is getting increasingly restless over this topic. Nobody knows how long they'll keep delaying the case."

286.speaker: Lucian Galade
286.text: "This, of course, allows Governor Bron to keep his seat and continue his resettlement policies in Bergia, among others."

287.speaker: Lucian Galade
287.text: "I'm afraid Chief Justice Hawker seems to be protecting Governor Bron from persecution. This will only increase tensions."

288.speaker: Lucian Galade
288.text: "Antagonizing him before the vote for the constitution was perhaps not the best idea."

289.speaker: Lucian Galade
289.text: "After you and Mr. Kibener made your statement in support of Sollist constitutionalism, the Supreme Court prioritized the case and quickly announced a verdict."

290.speaker: Lucian Galade
290.text: "It was very clever of you to use Sollism against them. They couldn't afford to look like hypocrites, so they must have moved on it very quickly."

291.speaker: Lucian Galade
291.text: "The Court ruled that Phelix Bron is to be relieved from his position as governor for abusing his powers to discriminate against Sordish citizens."

292.speaker: Lucian Galade
292.text: "He is banned from serving in any political positions in the future and will be charged with a fine of five million Sordish Ren."

293.speaker: Lucian Galade
293.text: "However, the Court has also rejected Ersen's arguments about the Constitution, ruling that all citizens of Sordland are Sords regardless of ethnicity and are completely equal before the law."

294.speaker: Lucian Galade
294.text: "The results received a mixed response from the Bludish community."

295.speaker: Lucian Galade
295.text: "The resettlements policies of Bergia are ruled to be unconstitutional and have been revoked."

296.speaker: Lucian Galade
296.text: "Activists, radicals and BFF sympathizers have condemned the ruling. However, the majority seems to recognize that justice has been served."

297.speaker: Lucian Galade
297.text: "We've just received word about the case of Ishval Ersen. The Supreme Court has decided not to act at all, and delayed the case indefinitely."

298.speaker: Lucian Galade
298.text: "I'm afraid Chief Justice Hawker seems to be protecting Governor Bron from persecution."

302.speaker: Player
302.text: "This is very troubling. Do you have any idea how we can proceed?"

303.speaker: Player
303.text: "Ms. Morgna was right about how extreme Mr. Hawker's opinions were. I should have known this would be the outcome."

304.speaker: Player
304.text: "Orso Hawker is going too far with this."

305.speaker: Lucian Galade
305.text: "There was nothing you could do, sir."

306.speaker: Lucian Galade
306.text: "He is. That's why taking away the Court's authority with our proposal was our highest priority."

307.speaker: Lucian Galade
307.text: "I don't think there is anything we can do about it at this point."

308.speaker: Lucian Galade
308.text: "Our strategy should be to get public opinion behind us."

309.speaker: Player
309.text: "Sollist or not, this is good news. Bergia will finally be free from Governor Bron's racist rule."

310.speaker: Player
310.text: "What more do these *activists* want? They only want to see the bad side of everything. Maybe Soll wasn't so wrong about his policies."

311.speaker: Player
311.text: "Thank you for informing me, Lucian. Do you have any idea on how we proceed?"

313.speaker: Lucian Galade
313.text: "As long as we can ride the aftermath of these results to our advantage, the fringe of Bludish society won't matter for us. They can't affect the vote too much."

314.speaker: Lucian Galade
314.text: "I don't think there's anything we need to do at this moment, sir."

315.speaker: Lucian Galade
315.text: "There is one more important detail. The seat of Governor of Bergia must be filled."

316.speaker: Lucian Galade
316.text: "Normally, the President appoints the Governor of the Special Zone directly. I'm afraid despite Ms. Morgna's protests, the Court decided to take a completely different route on this."

317.speaker: Lucian Galade
317.text: "Mr. Hawker argued that a premature departure of a governor during their term is an exceptional case. They ruled that the deputy of Governor Bron will assume his duty until the end of the term."

318.speaker: Lucian Galade
318.text: "Mr. Kibener might have played you, unfortunately. The deputy in question -- Mr. Krull -- is a member of the NFP. I'm afraid the Court delivered Bergia straight into the NFP's hands."

319.speaker: Player
319.text: "What!? How can they just decide to do that?"

320.speaker: Player
320.text: "I'm really questioning Ms. Morgna's advice on this now. She should have seen this coming."

321.speaker: Player
321.text: "This is very bad news. What do we do now?"

322.speaker: Player
322.text: "Screw Hawker! Screw Kibener! This whole system is broken!"

323.speaker: Lucian Galade
323.text: "And thanks to you, we are doing our best to fix it, sir."

324.speaker: Lucian Galade
324.text: "She's a competent woman, but she keeps underestimating the Old Guard. Her naive idealism gets the better of her at times."

325.speaker: Lucian Galade
325.text: "Unfortunately, there's nothing we can do about it, sir."

326.speaker: Lucian Galade
326.text: "Luckily, Mr. Krull will not be able to resume any of his predecessor's unconstitutional activities."

327.speaker: Lucian Galade
327.text: "Of course, giving such a powerful position to a far-right nationalist is still very concerning."

334.speaker: Lucian Galade
334.text: "Luckily, Ms. Graf is already working on the revocation of the Special Zone in Bergia. We may still be able to get rid of Mr. Krull that way."

335.speaker: Lucian Galade
335.text: "Luckily, Ms. Morgna is already working on the semi-autonomous zone in Bergia. We may still be able to get rid of Mr. Krull that way."

342.speaker: Lucian Galade
342.text: "It would likely be ready after the vote for the amendments."

343.speaker: Lucian Galade
343.text: "Luckily, Ms. Graf is already working on the revocation of the Special Zone in Bergia. We may still be able to get rid of the governor that way."

344.speaker: Lucian Galade
344.text: "Luckily, Ms. Morgna is already working on the semi-autonomous zone in Bergia. We may still be able to get rid of the governor that way."

345.speaker: Lucian Galade
345.text: "You'd be free to enact it then."

352.speaker: Lucian Galade
352.text: "However... There might be a problem with its timing. It would likely only be ready after the vote for the amendments."

353.speaker: Lucian Galade
353.text: "If the vote succeeds as we've been working for, we'd be removing all of your authority to enact presidential decrees."

354.speaker: Lucian Galade
354.text: "I'm afraid you'll need the approval of the Assembly in that scenario."

355.speaker: Lucian Galade
355.text: "And I doubt they'll support any change to Mr. Bron's special authority. He's been a very important member of the party, as well as an important... fundraiser."

356.speaker: Lucian Galade
356.text: "However... There might be a problem with its timing. It would likely only be ready after the vote for the amendments."

357.speaker: Lucian Galade
357.text: "If the vote succeeds as we've been working for, your limited decree powers won't be enough to enact a change this grand."

358.speaker: Lucian Galade
358.text: "As hesitant as I am to support your decision to include changes to Article 6 and 7 in your proposal at this stage, it might allow us to bring him to justice, if the vote succeeds."

359.speaker: Lucian Galade
359.text: "Ms. Morgna has informed me that most of the work on the wording is already done and she had reached out to the representatives of the Bludish community to get their input."

360.speaker: Lucian Galade
360.text: "If you are insistent on adding this change to our proposal, we can discuss this in detail when the representatives arrive."

361.speaker: Lucian Galade
361.text: "It would likely be ready after the vote for the amendments."

362.speaker: Lucian Galade
362.text: "You'd be free to enact it then."

369.speaker: Lucian Galade
369.text: "However... There might be a problem with its timing. It would likely be ready after the vote for the amendments."

370.speaker: Lucian Galade
370.text: "If the vote succeeds as we've been working for, we'd be removing all of your authority to enact presidential decrees."

371.speaker: Lucian Galade
371.text: "However... There might be a problem with its timing. It would likely be ready after the vote for the amendments."

372.speaker: Lucian Galade
372.text: "If the vote succeeds as we've been working for, your limited decree powers won't be enough to enact a change this grand."

376.speaker: Lucian Galade
376.text: "Unfortunately, changing Articles 6 and 7 is no longer a possibility. After your statements to pressure the Court, the mood has shifted quite a bit."

377.speaker: Lucian Galade
377.text: "But there is not much we can do about it at the moment."

378.speaker: Lucian Galade
378.text: "Ms. Morgna has informed me that the Bludish movement has pulled their support from the committee."

380.speaker: Player
380.text: "This is ridiculous. Tell her to work faster. It needs to be finished before the vote."

381.speaker: Player
381.text: "I'm sure we can find a way to convince the party by then."

382.speaker: Player
382.text: "Well... who knows whether our reforms will pass."

383.speaker: Lucian Galade
383.text: "For the sake of our administration, I certainly hope they do."

385.speaker: Lucian Galade
385.text: "I'll tell her immediately after our meeting, sir. But I don't think it will make any difference."

386.speaker: Lucian Galade
386.text: "The representatives of the Bludish community -- namely Mansoun Leke and Fetih Ejall -- have just informed me that they wish to meet with you."
386.conditionsRaw:
((Variable["BaseGame.BergiaSpecialZone_Proposal_Amendment"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Bill_Turn05_ReligiousHarmony_Signed"] == false  and  (Variable["BaseGame.Bill_Turn01_CampaignFinance_Signed"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Wehlen_DefendBorder"] == true) == false  and 
Variable["BaseGame.Wehlen_JointOperation"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Reform_NFP_Convinced"] == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.ErsenCase_Statement_ProBlud"] == true)

387.speaker: Lucian Galade
387.text: "They also wanted me to relay their surprise and support for your statement in defense of Ishval Ersen. After all, not every USP president calls the constitution racist."

388.speaker: Lucian Galade
388.text: "This might have made them soften up to you. If you accept the meeting, it would be the first ever meeting between the WPB and a standing president. A major event for their community."

389.speaker: Player
389.text: "Great news. Tell her I'm grateful for her work on this."

391.speaker: Player
391.text: "Good to know. I'm looking forward to signing it."

392.speaker: Lucian Galade
392.text: "We should use every future opportunity we get to increase our standing with the Bludish community. They may have a considerable influence on the elections."

393.speaker: Player
393.text: "I'm not doing this for the elections, Lucian."

395.speaker: Player
395.text: "I don't think their influence is large enough for us to care."

396.speaker: Lucian Galade
396.text: "Their numbers are not that large, but they might make a critical difference if we lose the favor of the general public."

397.speaker: Lucian Galade
397.text: "But I agree, sir. Flirting with the Bludish community only results in more loss from the nationalists. We cannot afford to do that."

400.speaker: Lucian Galade
400.text: "I am not sure exactly which topics they want to bring up. But we can talk about that later."

402.speaker: Lucian Galade
402.text: "I'm afraid you won't be able to enact this change without the approval of the Assembly in that scenario."

403.speaker: Lucian Galade
403.text: "It will be very hard to convince them to revoke the Special Zone. But with Mr. Bron -- an important fundraiser for the USP -- gone, the party may be willing to move against Governor Krull."

404.speaker: Player
404.text: "This is ridiculous. Tell her to work faster. It needs to be finished before the vote."

405.speaker: Player
405.text: "I'm sure we can find a way to convince the party by then."

406.speaker: Player
406.text: "Well... It's not certain our reforms will pass."

407.speaker: Lucian Galade
407.text: "We have to make sure that doesn't happen for the sake of our administration."

409.speaker: Lucian Galade
409.text: "I'll tell her immediately after our meeting, sir. But I don't think that will make any difference."

410.speaker: Player
410.text: "Great news. Tell her I'm grateful for her work on this."

412.speaker: Player
412.text: "Good to know. I'm looking forward to signing it."

413.speaker: Player
413.text: "This is worrying. We must look to other ways to increase our standing with our Bludish community."

414.speaker: Player
414.text: "I don't think this is a negative result. I'm sure Mr. Krull will do a good job."

415.speaker: Player
415.text: "This is bad news, Lucian. This was not my intention."

416.speaker: Lucian Galade
416.text: "We'll congratulate him when he assumes office."

418.speaker: Lucian Galade
418.text: "There's no use pondering on the past, sir. We can still find other ways to help the Bludish community."

421.speaker: Narrator
421.text: He took a look at his watch.

422.speaker: Player
422.text: "I'm sure this is a positive development. I'd be happy to meet them."

423.speaker: Player
423.text: "Do you think I should accept their meeting?"

424.speaker: Player
424.text: "I don't want to be seen with them right before the vote. This can be detrimental for us."

426.speaker: Lucian Galade
426.text: "They haven't officially reached out yet. When they do, it will be up to you whether you want to listen to them or not."

428.speaker: Lucian Galade
428.text: "It might be risky being seen with the leader of the WPB before the vote, but it's worth hearing them out."

429.speaker: Lucian Galade
429.text: "I don't think we should outright ignore our Bludish community. However, I have to note that this is a very risky move."

430.speaker: Player
430.text: "That's great news. I'm looking forward to discussing the changes."

432.speaker: Player
432.text: "I'm not completely sure if I'm going to add that to the proposal yet. I'll decide on the meeting."

434.speaker: Lucian Galade
434.text: "I'm afraid it would be almost impossible to pass this change. I don't think it is worth tanking our reforms."

435.speaker: Lucian Galade
435.text: "It is still not too late to cancel the meeting. But if you do decide to meet them, I'll be there to discuss everything in detail."

436.speaker: Lucian Galade
436.text: "No harm done, sir. It would have been impossible to pass our reforms with these."

437.speaker: Lucian Galade
437.text: "For now, let's return back to the real reason we are here. Our economic direction."

440.speaker: Lucian Galade
440.text: "I'm afraid it will be very bad press to be seen with the current and former leaders of the WPB."

441.speaker: Player
441.text: "We should paint Mr. Krull as a threat to the party's rule. I believe we can take advantage of partisanship and get them behind us."

442.speaker: Lucian Galade
442.text: "Of course. That's a clever strategy, sir."

444.speaker: Lucian Galade
444.text: "You can always reject their meeting altogether of course, so we don't lose support among Sordish nationalists."

445.speaker: Player
445.text: "They pull out after we include them in the process? So be it. I'm done fighting for them."

446.speaker: Player
446.text: "Not great. But it would probably have been worse for us if we included those changes at the last minute."

447.speaker: Lucian Galade
447.text: "These changes were not part of our initial proposal and target, sir. I don't think much has changed."

479.speaker: Lucian Galade
479.text: "The representatives of the Bludish community -- namely Mansoun Leke and Fetih Ejall -- have just released statements condemning our administration."

480.speaker: Lucian Galade
480.text: "They criticized your inactions on the Ersen case. And they used a very strong language doing so, I must add."

481.speaker: Lucian Galade
481.text: "They have enormous influence over our Bludish population. Just something to be aware of."

486.speaker: Lucian Galade
486.text: "Ms. Morgna has informed me that the representatives of the Bludish community have abandoned the reform committee after the developments regarding the Ersen case."

487.speaker: Lucian Galade
487.text: "The proposal was unfortunately not finalized yet -- meaning that changes to Articles 6 and 7 must be delayed for the time being."

489.speaker: Player
489.text: "I wasn't sure if I was going to add that to our reform proposal anyway."

491.speaker: Lucian Galade
491.text: "They criticized both you and the Supreme Court for protecting Sollism."

492.speaker: Lucian Galade
492.text: "I don't think they are convinced to cooperate with us, sir."

493.speaker: Lucian Galade
493.text: "But I have to say that this turned out to be a better outcome. Adding those changes to the reforms would have been disastrous."

494.speaker: Lucian Galade
494.text: "They criticized your cooperation with the NFP and called your pro-Ersen statement 'an attempt of populist manipulation'."

498.speaker: Lucian Galade
498.text: "Despite showing support after your statements about Ishval Ersen, the representatives of the Bludish community -- namely Mansoun Leke and Fetih Ejall -- have just released statements condemning our administration."

499.speaker: Lucian Galade
499.text: "They criticized your policies against the Bludish community and called your pro-Ersen statement 'a poor attempt of tricking the Bludish people'."
